verses.1:1: The burden that Habakkuk the prophet saw.
verses.1:2: How long, O Lord, shall I cry out, and You will not hear? Shall I cry aloud to You while suffering wrong, and will You not save?
verses.1:3: Why have You shown me troubles and toils to look upon, wretchedness and ungodliness? Judgment has come against me, and the judge receives;
verses.1:4: therefore the law is annulled, and justice is not carried through to the end, for the ungodly oppresses the righteous; on account of this, justice shall go forth perverted.
verses.1:5: Look, you despisers, and gaze, and marvel at wondrous things, and vanish away; for I am performing a work in your days which you will by no means believe, even if one recounts it in full.
verses.1:6: For behold, I am raising up the Chaldeans, that bitter and swift nation, which marches across the breadths of the earth to inherit dwellings not its own;
verses.1:7: terrible and illustrious is he; from himself shall his judgment be, and his burden shall go forth from himself;
verses.1:8: and his horses shall leap swifter than leopards, and are fiercer than the wolves of Arabia; and his horsemen shall ride forth and rush from afar, and they shall fly as an eagle eager to devour.
verses.1:9: Consummation shall come upon the ungodly, who resist with their faces set opposite, and he shall gather captivity as sand.
verses.1:10: And he shall make sport of kings, and tyrants shall be his playthings; and he shall mock at every stronghold, and cast up a mound and seize it.
verses.1:11: Then he shall change his spirit, and pass through, and make atonement; this strength belongs to my God.
verses.1:12: Are You not from the beginning, O Lord God, my Holy One? Surely we shall by no means die. O Lord, You have appointed it for judgment; and He formed me to reprove His chastening.
verses.1:13: Pure is Your eye, so as not to behold evil things, nor to look upon toils of anguish; why do You look upon those who despise? Will You keep silent while the ungodly swallows up the righteous?
verses.1:14: And will You make men like the fish of the sea, and like the creeping things that have no ruler?
verses.1:15: He has drawn up consummation with a hook, and dragged him in a casting net, and gathered him in his dragnets. On account of this his heart shall be glad and rejoice;
verses.1:16: on account of this he shall sacrifice to his dragnet and burn incense to his casting net, because by them he has made his portion fat and his foods choice;
verses.1:17: therefore he shall cast his casting net, and he shall not spare to slay nations continually.
verses.2:1: Upon my watch I will stand, and I will mount upon a rock, and I will watch intently to see what He will speak in me, and what I shall answer concerning my reproof.
verses.2:2: And the Lord answered me and said, "Write a vision, and plainly upon a tablet, so that he who reads these things may run.
verses.2:3: For the vision is yet for an appointed time, and it shall spring up at the end and not in vain; if he delays, wait patiently for him, for he shall surely come, and shall by no means tarry.
verses.2:4: If he draws back, My soul has no pleasure in him; but the righteous shall live by My faithfulness.
verses.2:5: Now the arrogant man is a despiser; he shall accomplish nothing, who has enlarged his soul like Hades, and he, like death, is never satisfied; and he shall gather to himself all the nations, and shall receive to himself all the peoples.
verses.2:6: Shall not all these take up a proverb against him, and a riddle for a tale concerning him? And they shall say, 'Woe to him who multiplies for himself what is not his—how long?—and who heavily weighs down his collar!
verses.2:7: For suddenly those who bite him shall rise up, and those who plot against you shall awake, and you shall become plunder for them.
verses.2:8: Because you have plundered many nations, all the remaining peoples shall take plunder, because of the blood of men and the ungodliness of the land, and of the city, and of all who dwell in it.'
verses.2:9: Woe to him who covets an evil gain for his house, to set his nest on high, to be snatched away from the hand of evils;
verses.2:10: you have devised shame for your house, you have made an end of many peoples, and your soul has sinned;
verses.2:11: for a stone shall cry out from the wall, and the beetle from the timber shall speak of these things.
verses.2:12: Woe to him who builds a city with bloodshed, and establishes a city with iniquities.
verses.2:13: Are not these things from the Lord Almighty? And many peoples have failed in the fire, and many nations have grown fainthearted.
verses.2:14: For the earth shall be filled to know the glory of the Lord, as water shall cover them.
verses.2:15: Woe to him who gives his neighbor to drink with a turbid overturning, and makes him drunk, so that he may gaze upon their caverns.
verses.2:16: Drink also yourself a fullness of dishonor instead of glory; be shaken in heart and tremble; the cup of the right hand of the Lord has come around to you, and dishonor has been gathered upon your glory.
verses.2:17: For the ungodliness of Lebanon shall cover you, and the wretchedness of wild beasts shall terrify you, because of the blood of men and the ungodliness of the land, and of the city, and of all who dwell in it.
verses.2:18: What does a carved image profit, that they have carved it? He has fashioned it as a molten image, a false apparition, because he who fashioned it has trusted in his own handiwork, to make mute idols.
verses.2:19: Woe to him who says to the wood, 'Awake, arise!' and to the stone, 'Be exalted!' Yet it is an apparition; and this is a plating of gold and silver, and there is no breath at all in it.
verses.2:20: But the Lord is in His holy temple; let all the earth stand in awe before His presence."
verses.3:1: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, with a song.
verses.3:2: O Lord, I have heard Your report, and I was afraid; I considered Your works, and I was amazed. In the midst of two living creatures You shall be known; as the years draw near, You shall be recognized; when the appointed time arrives, You shall be revealed; when my soul is troubled, in wrath You shall remember mercy.
verses.3:3: God shall come from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran, shady and densely wooded. Interlude. His excellence covered the heavens, and the earth is full of His praise.
verses.3:4: And His radiance shall be as the light; horns are in His hands, and He has established a mighty love of His strength.
verses.3:5: Before His face a word shall go, and it shall go forth into the plains at His feet.
verses.3:6: He stood, and the earth was shaken; He looked, and the nations melted away; the mountains were shattered with violence, the everlasting hills melted along His everlasting ways.
verses.3:7: Because of troubles I saw the dwellings of the Ethiopians; the tents of the land of Midian shall also be terrified.
verses.3:8: Were You angry with the rivers, O Lord? Or was Your wrath against the rivers? Or Your onslaught against the sea? For You shall mount upon Your horses, and Your riding is salvation.
verses.3:9: Bending, You bent Your bow against scepters, says the Lord. Interlude. The earth shall be split with rivers;
verses.3:10: peoples shall see You and be in travail. Scattering the waters of the course, the abyss uttered its voice, the height of its apparition.
verses.3:11: The sun was lifted up, and the moon stood in its order; into the light Your darts shall go forth, at the radiance of the lightning of Your weapons.
verses.3:12: With threatening You shall diminish the earth, and in wrath You shall bring down the nations;
verses.3:13: You went forth for the salvation of Your people, to save Your anointed one; You shall cast death upon the heads of the lawless; You have raised up bonds even to the neck. Interlude.
verses.3:14: You cut asunder in amazement the heads of the mighty; they shall be shaken in it; they shall open their bridles as a poor man eating in secret.
verses.3:15: And You mount Your horses into the sea, troubling much water.
verses.3:16: I kept watch, and my belly was terrified at the voice of the prayer of my lips, and trembling entered into my bones, and beneath me my frame was troubled. I shall rest in the day of affliction, to go up to the people of my sojourning.
verses.3:17: For the fig tree shall not bear fruit, and there shall be no produce on the vines; the labor of the olive tree shall fail, and the plains shall yield no food; the sheep have failed from food, and there are no oxen at the mangers.
verses.3:18: Yet I will exult in the Lord; I will rejoice in God my Savior.
verses.3:19: The Lord God is my strength, and He shall set my feet to perfection; He causes me to mount upon the high places, to conquer in His song.

notes.1:3: Greek 'and the judge receives' (καὶ ὁ κριτὴς λαμβάνει) is elliptical, implying the taking of bribes or partiality, and diverges from the Masoretic Text's reference to strife and contention.
notes.1:8: The Greek reads 'the wolves of Arabia' (τοὺς λύκους τῆς Ἀραβίας), reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants rendered 'evening wolves' in the Masoretic Text.
notes.1:11: Unlike the Masoretic Text ('and be guilty, whose own might is his god'), the Greek reads 'and make atonement; this strength belongs to my God' (καὶ ἐξιλάσεται· αὕτη ἡ ἰσχὺς τῷ θεῷ μου).
notes.1:12: The Greek shifts to the third person ('He formed me to reprove His chastening'), reading the Hebrew consonantal root for 'Rock' as the verb 'to form.'
notes.2:3: The Greek shifts from the feminine noun 'vision' (ὅρασις) to the masculine pronoun 'him' (αὐτόν) and participle 'coming' (ἐρχόμενος), forming the basis for the messianic quotation in Hebrews 10:37.
notes.2:4: The Greek reads 'by My faithfulness' (ἐκ πίστεώς μου, also translatable 'by My faith') rather than the Masoretic Text's 'by his faithfulness,' and opens with 'if he draws back, My soul has no pleasure in him' (cf. Hebrews 10:38).
notes.2:11: Greek κάνθαρος literally means 'beetle' ('the beetle from the timber'), differing from the Masoretic Text's architectural 'beam' or 'rafter.'
notes.2:14: Unlike the Masoretic Text ('as the waters cover the sea'), the Greek concludes with 'as water shall cover them' (ὡς ὕδωρ κατακαλύψει αὐτούς).
notes.2:15: Greek τὰ σπήλαια αὐτῶν literally means 'their caverns' (reading the Hebrew consonants for 'nakedness' as 'caves'), and ἀνατροπῇ θολερᾷ denotes a 'turbid overturning.'
notes.3:2: Renowned in early Christian exegesis, the Greek reads 'in the midst of two living creatures You shall be known' (ἐν μέσῳ δύο ζῴων γνωσθήσῃ), differing from the Masoretic Text's 'in the midst of the years revive it.'
notes.3:3: Greek διάψαλμα ('Interlude,' also in 3:9 and 3:13) is the Septuagint musical direction corresponding to Hebrew Selah.
notes.3:5: The Greek reads 'a word' (λόγος), vocalizing the Hebrew consonantal text for 'pestilence' as 'word.'
notes.3:7: Greek Αἰθιόπων ('Ethiopians') is the Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew proper name Cushan.
notes.3:19: The Greek reads 'to perfection' (εἰς συντέλειαν) rather than the Masoretic Text's 'like deer's feet,' and incorporates the concluding Hebrew musical notation into the prayer as 'to conquer in His song' (τοῦ νικῆσαι ἐν τῇ ᾠδῇ αὐτοῦ).
